chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from al-Raba'i, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in that:
If a man divorces his slave woman with two divorces and then buys her back, he said: No (it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her by ownership) until she marries another husband.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master divorces his slave woman twice and then buys her back?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific ruling for a slave woman divorced twice by her master, requiring an intervening marriage to a third party before he can reclaim her through purchase, mirroring the 'talaq al-thalatha' rule for free women. It highlights the distinct legal status of slave women in Shia jurisprudence, where the mechanism of re-acquisition via purchase is subject to the same marital barriers as free women to prevent immediate re-marriage without a genuine new union.
